title: Graphene and Fullerenes
content:
# Graphene and Fullerenes

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
- Describe the structures of graphene and fullerenes
- Explain the properties of graphene
- Describe the structure and uses of buckminsterfullerene (C₆₀)
- Explain the uses of carbon nanotubes

## Introduction

Graphene and fullerenes are relatively recently discovered forms of carbon with remarkable properties. They have revolutionised materials science and have potential applications in electronics, medicine, and engineering.

## Key Concepts

### Allotropes of Carbon

**Allotropes** are different physical forms of the same element. Carbon has several allotropes:

| Allotrope | Structure |
|-----------|-----------|
| Diamond | 3D tetrahedral network |
| Graphite | Stacked hexagonal layers |
| Graphene | Single hexagonal layer |
| Fullerenes | Spheres or tubes of carbon |

### Graphene

**Graphene** is a single layer of graphite - a one-atom-thick sheet of carbon atoms arranged in hexagons.

**Structure:**
- Single layer of carbon atoms
- Each carbon bonded to 3 others
- Hexagonal arrangement (like chicken wire)
- One delocalised electron per carbon atom
- The thinnest material known (one atom thick)

[DIAGRAM: Graphene structure showing hexagonal arrangement of carbon atoms]

**Properties:**

| Property | Description | Why? |
|----------|-------------|------|
| Extremely strong | 200× stronger than steel | Strong covalent bonds in all directions |
| Very light | Lightest known material | Only one atom thick |
| Excellent electrical conductor | Better than copper | Delocalised electrons |
| Excellent thermal conductor | Conducts heat very well | Delocalised electrons |
| Flexible | Can be bent without breaking | Single layer can flex |
| Transparent | Almost invisible | Only one atom thick |

**Potential uses of graphene:**
- Flexible touchscreens
- Ultra-fast electronics
- Lightweight composite materials
- Water filtration membranes
- Medical sensors
- Solar cells

### Fullerenes

**Fullerenes** are molecules of carbon atoms with hollow shapes - either spheres or tubes.

### Buckminsterfullerene (C₆₀)

**Structure:**
- 60 carbon atoms arranged in a sphere
- Shape like a football (soccer ball)
- Made of hexagons and pentagons
- Each carbon bonded to 3 others
- Has delocalised electrons

[DIAGRAM: C₆₀ buckminsterfullerene showing spherical structure]

**Properties:**
- Cage-like structure
- Can trap other atoms or molecules inside
- Relatively stable molecule
- Dissolves in some organic solvents

**Uses of buckminsterfullerene:**
- Drug delivery (trap drugs inside, deliver to specific cells)
- Lubricants
- Catalysts
- Superconductors
- Electronics

### Carbon Nanotubes

**Carbon nanotubes** are cylindrical fullerenes - essentially rolled-up sheets of graphene.

**Structure:**
- Tube of hexagonally arranged carbon atoms
- Each carbon bonded to 3 others
- Can be single-walled or multi-walled
- Delocalised electrons along the tube
- Very high length-to-diameter ratio

[DIAGRAM: Carbon nanotube structure]

**Properties:**

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Strength | 100× stronger than steel (same weight) |
| Conductivity | Excellent (better than copper) |
| Flexibility | Can bend without breaking |
| Diameter | About 1 nanometre |

**Uses of carbon nanotubes:**
- Reinforcing materials (composite materials)
- Electronics (tiny circuits)
- Computer chips
- Drug delivery systems
- Sports equipment (tennis rackets, bicycles)
- Building materials
- Nanotechnology

### Comparing Carbon Allotropes

| Property | Diamond | Graphite | Graphene | C₆₀ | Nanotubes |
|----------|---------|----------|----------|-----|----------|
| Bonds per C | 4 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| Structure | 3D network | Layers | Single layer | Sphere | Tube |
| Conducts? | No | Yes | Yes | Limited | Yes |
| Hardness | Very hard | Soft | Strong sheet | Soft solid | Very strong |

### Why These Materials Are Important

Graphene and fullerenes represent a new area of science called **nanotechnology** - working with materials at the atomic and molecular scale.

Advantages of nanomaterials:
- Unique properties not found in bulk materials
- Very high surface area to volume ratio
- Can be engineered for specific purposes

## Common Mistakes

- **Mistake:** Thinking graphene is a different element from graphite
- **Correct:** Both are allotropes of carbon - same element, different structure

- **Mistake:** Thinking carbon nanotubes are solid rods
- **Correct:** Carbon nanotubes are hollow tubes (like rolled graphene)

- **Mistake:** Confusing C₆₀ with a giant covalent structure
- **Correct:** C₆₀ is a molecule (contains exactly 60 atoms)

## Practice Questions

1. Describe the structure of graphene. (3 marks)

2. Explain why graphene can conduct electricity. (2 marks)

3. State two properties of graphene that make it useful for making flexible electronic screens. (2 marks)

4. Describe the structure of buckminsterfullerene (C₆₀). (2 marks)

5. Carbon nanotubes are used to strengthen sports equipment such as tennis rackets. Explain why carbon nanotubes are suitable for this use. (3 marks)

6. Suggest why fullerenes can be used to deliver drugs to specific parts of the body. (3 marks)

## Key Terms Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| Allotrope | Different physical forms of the same element |
| Graphene | A single layer of carbon atoms arranged in hexagons |
| Fullerene | A molecule of carbon atoms with a hollow sphere or tube shape |
| Buckminsterfullerene | C₆₀ - a spherical molecule of 60 carbon atoms |
| Carbon nanotube | A cylindrical fullerene made of rolled graphene |
| Nanotechnology | Science and engineering at the nanometre scale |

## Summary

- **Graphene** is a single layer of graphite (one atom thick)
  - Very strong, conducts electricity, flexible, transparent
  - Uses: flexible screens, electronics, composites

- **Buckminsterfullerene (C₆₀)** is a spherical molecule of 60 carbon atoms
  - Cage structure can trap other molecules
  - Uses: drug delivery, catalysts, lubricants

- **Carbon nanotubes** are cylindrical fullerenes (rolled graphene)
  - Very strong, excellent conductors
  - Uses: reinforcing materials, electronics, nanotechnology

- All have delocalised electrons (each carbon bonds to only 3 others)
- These materials are important for future technologies
